articles.title: Should AI crawlers access your site?
articles.excerpt: Many sites added Disallow: / for GPTBot in 2023 and never looked at it again. Some went further and blocked every AI user agent they could find. That is a legitimate choice. But it is often made witho…
articles.body: Many sites added Disallow: / for GPTBot in 2023 and never looked at it again. Some went further and blocked every AI user agent they could find. That is a legitimate choice. But it is often made without knowing that the crawlers do different jobs. Block the training bot and you keep your content out of training. Block the search bot and you may vanish from AI answers. This guide separates the two so you can decide on purpose. The core idea: one company, several bots OpenAI, Anthropic and Perplexity each run more than one user agent. Their own documentation splits them by purpose, and each is controlled separately in robots.txt. OpenAI Per OpenAI's crawler documentation, there are these robots: GPTBot crawls content that may be used to train OpenAI's generative AI foundation models.

articles.title: I built a site chatbot that isn't allowed to make things up
articles.excerpt: In 2024 a tribunal in Canada made Air Canada honor what its website chatbot had told a customer about refunds. The airline argued the bot was responsible for its own words. The tribunal said the compa…
articles.body: In 2024 a tribunal in Canada made Air Canada honor what its website chatbot had told a customer about refunds. The airline argued the bot was responsible for its own words. The tribunal said the company is responsible for everything on its site, chatbot included. For a small business that is the real problem with site chatbots. A wrong opening time or an invented price costs more than the bot saves. So I built a demo where the model is only allowed to draft, and plain code decides what the customer sees: Front Desk . The setup The demo runs on Juniper Street Bakery, a bakery I made up. Its whole "site" is 13 short entries: hours, prices, cakes, allergens, delivery, payment. The assistant knows nothing else. The model is Gemma 4 E2B, running in the browser through WebLLM at temperature 0.

articles.title: When the Jiusion head will not settle
articles.excerpt: What this head will not do I keep a Jiusion 1600X USB microscope for marks my eyes miss. It is a close viewer, and I have stopped asking it to behave like a bench instrument. The sensor is a VGA chip,…
articles.body: What this head will not do I keep a Jiusion 1600X USB microscope for marks my eyes miss. It is a close viewer, and I have stopped asking it to behave like a bench instrument. The sensor is a VGA chip, 640 by 480, and the moving picture stays around thirty frames in a second. A saved frame leaves as a BMP file or a JPEG file. That is the whole of what I expect from it. The ruler packed with it helps me line a subject up. I do not treat a reading off that ruler as something I would put my name under. When the lamps flood the metal There are eight lamps in a ring at the lens. A coin rewards that light: an edge, a date, a mint mark. A solder pad and a charging socket do the opposite. The metal flares white.

articles.title: Firefox Privacy Settings: A Practical Guide (Not Paranoia-Level)
articles.excerpt: Most Firefox privacy guides go one of two ways: "just enable Strict Mode" (too shallow) or "change 50 about:config settings" (too much). Here's a practical middle ground — what actually matters, what…
articles.body: Most Firefox privacy guides go one of two ways: "just enable Strict Mode" (too shallow) or "change 50 about:config settings" (too much). Here's a practical middle ground — what actually matters, what the tradeoffs are. Start: Enhanced Tracking Protection Go to about:preferences#privacy and look at "Enhanced Tracking Protection." Three settings: Standard — blocks social media trackers, cross-site tracking cookies, fingerprinters in private windows Strict — adds tracking content blockers, more fingerprint resistance, blocks more trackers. Some sites may break. Custom — fine-tune what's blocked Recommendation: Start with Strict. If a site breaks, you can click the shield icon in the address bar and disable ETP for just that site. The number of sites that break is lower than people expect.

articles.title: 34 Years Later, the Best-Ever 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
articles.excerpt: Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was known for its visual humor, but this is the best-ever quote from the series
articles.body: Larson didn’t do deep . He didn’t do inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful in the lofty sense. They required thought because Larson’s work was brilliant, and you sometimes had to figure out what the punchline was. For example, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly on his glasses. Larson’s work often requires the reader to investigate something, but usually not in any kind of overly deep way.

articles.body: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. Of course, there are classics with years of literary study behind them that speak volumes on the nature of society, technology, or the world writ large. But few are quite as elegant or as profoundly humanistic as the final moments of Arkady and Boris Strugatsky’s Roadside Picnic . The 1972 novel offers a very different kind of sci-fi ending than its myriad predecessors and successors.

articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 .
